## Summary (human-written)
<!-- Write this yourself, not with an AI tool. 2-5 sentences: the problem, why
     this approach, and what you checked yourself. -->

## Rebase and review status

Current head: `cbe9b3c8636932fb2a8a7e40dd0b1c2377241d71`. The stack is rebased onto fetched upstream main
`73c4ebdac57de0d89bb20d5dfabed340449c8b0d`; commit prefixes now match the four PR titles.
The latest `pr-review` skill and checklist were read from this rebased checkout.

The rebase updates the `PrecisionConfig` parallelize contract, checks QSA
accelerator capture before dynamic metadata construction, preserves Flash-Next's
BF16 GDN parameter policy, restores the PP test imports, and retains upstream's
redundant-test deletions. Current exact-prefix checks: all-file pre-commit passes
and 51 CPU tests pass. The full-stack CPU run hides GPUs so the
upstream CPU FSDP test does not select the unavailable FA4 package.

[Claude's review of #5782](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5782#pullrequestreview-5761648327)
still has open FSDP/indexer and QSA training-memory findings. Earlier local
approval claims are withdrawn. HF/GPU/convergence results below are historical
captures at their stated SHAs; this rebase has not received fresh GPU validation.
The human summary placeholder is retained for the author to complete before review.

## Why

The preceding model PR rejects TP and EP. Flash-Next needs its four-stream
residuals and full-history PLE to follow the shared activation placements, and
its TP-replicated indexer must receive one globally normalized teacher update.
This PR supplies those sharding contracts using the existing SPMD/FSDP bridge.

For TP2/SP, PLE gathers token history and lexical feature shards before computing
its document-local update, then returns each token shard:

```text
residual rank 0: [T/2, 4D] -- gather -- PLE [T, 4D] -- return rank 0 tokens
residual rank 1: [T/2, 4D] -- gather -- PLE [T, 4D] -- return rank 1 tokens
lexical table:   [rows, F/2] per TP rank -> lookup -> gathered [T, heads, F]
teacher heads:  sum across TP -> block maximum -> replicated indexer KL
```

## What changed

- Enable TP1/TP2 with and without SP, and EP, through declarative model sharding.
  Reject degrees that split the two QSA KV heads before model construction.
- Preserve identical versus token-varying TP gradient semantics for grouped
  norms and unsharded linears; shard lexical-table features across TP.
- Sum teacher heads before block max pooling and count replicated indexer
  gradients once. Reduce detached teachers in packets of 16 query chunks
  (256 queries by default) while preserving SDPA and KL accumulation order.
- Add the TP2/EP2/SP debug recipe and a 273-token CPU oracle covering the
  256-query packet boundary, tail probabilities and TP gradient scaling.

PP and CP remain explicitly unsupported at this increment. This PR depends on
`[qwen3_8_fn] 1/n`.

## User-facing changes

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Flash-Next rejects `tensor_parallel_degree=2` / `expert_parallel_degree=2` | The TP2/EP2 recipe runs with sequence parallelism and SPMD typechecking |
| PLE needs the full token history on each layer invocation | Its SP path gathers the original history and lexical-feature shards, then returns the local token slice |
| All nontrivial TP degrees are rejected | TP1/TP2 are supported; TP4 reports the QSA KV-head divisibility error while building the model |

## Numerics

The offline matrix uses one FP32 checkpoint, eight logical 64-token documents,
512 routing tokens and 504 CE tokens. All 190 reconstructed preclip parameter
gradients pass unchanged BF16 RMS/infinity bounds (`atol=1e-4`, `rtol=0.03125`);
all natural MoE/QSA sets agree. Replicas are checked exactly and counted once.
There is no fitted gradient rescaling. The exact-prefix captures were made at
`6bc85a249998f5ed4e1295143ad836324f6184be`; its amendment only adds early
rejection of invalid TP degrees and the associated CPU check/documentation.
Every valid TP1/TP2 config and forward/backward equation is unchanged.

| Layout | Global gradient norm ratio | Global cosine |
| --- | --- | --- |
| FSDP2 | 0.999999999996 | 1.0 |
| FSDP2/EP2 | 1.000000102204 | 0.999999990711 |
| TP2/EP2, SP disabled | 1.000062851570 | 0.999959733804 |
| TP2/EP2/SP | 1.000164114499 | 0.999959747135 |

The fixed native-choice checkpoint includes a separately disclosed conditioning
fixture. It fixes lexical feature zero to 1 and the corresponding key-projection
row in each stream to gain 0.125. That gain was selected using forward-only
criteria before observing its distributed gradients: raw key/query dot >= 1
and sigmoid(signed sqrt) <= 0.9. Actual GPU forwards satisfy raw minimum
1.0390625 and gate maximum 0.875 on all tokens/streams. Production math,
reference weights, C4 weights and comparison bounds are unchanged.

The original near-zero fixture is retained: one SP table entry exceeded its
original peak bound by 1.4%. Captured lookup vectors and token ownership agree
exactly; local VJPs attribute the difference to BF16 query drift amplified by
the signed-square-root gate near zero. The conditioned fixture checks placement
and normalization; it is not a claim of universal BF16 pointwise parity.

The teacher-packet refactor additionally passes a same-layout, same-checkpoint
10-step comparison on two GB300 GPUs, TP2/EP2/SP, seed 42, strict deterministic:
full-precision loss and gradient norm are bitwise identical under
`scripts/loss_compare.py --metrics loss,grad_norm --assert-equal`. Its local
before/after refs are `a43b124f8176d53c385bcdd2867b53f1f29dfe45` and
`4b2997e803b766f3b60d51cb580568a109d2ca51`; their sole difference is teacher
batching in `QSAInnerAttention.forward`. Those historical refs qualify the teacher-packet change and later TP4
rejection. The earlier logger migration is retained. The current base and
CPU/lint checks are listed separately above; GPU qualification is pending.
This PR makes no measured throughput claim.

## Testing

Current rebased prefix: `cbe9b3c8636932fb2a8a7e40dd0b1c2377241d71`. Its all-file pre-commit hooks and
51 CPU config/feature cases pass. Numerical captures below retain
their original source references.

- Exact-prefix pre-commit: all hooks pass.
- CPU feature/config tests: 51 pass, including the cross-packet oracle and
  explicit TP4 rejection for every flavor.
- Fixed-checkpoint real FSDP2, EP2, TP2/EP2 with SP off/on: all 190 gradients pass.
- Ten-step teacher batching loss/grad_norm comparison: bitwise equal.
- The TP4 configuration check is retained. Parent #5782 still has open FSDP/indexer and QSA saved-memory findings; the earlier local approval claim is withdrawn.

```bash
NGPU=2 MODULE=torchtitan_recipes.tests.models.qwen3_8_flash_next \
  CONFIG=qwen38_flash_next_debugmodel_tp2 ./run_train.sh
pytest tests/unit_tests/cpu/models/test_qwen3_8_flash_next.py -q
```

Full-size sparse throughput/memory and distributed conversion of the released
51.2B lexical table remain unvalidated. The next PR fixes shared GDN deterministic
normalization; pipeline support and combined remote integration follow in 4/n.

## Stack

This stack supersedes [the earlier all-in-one draft #5655](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5655).
Its original branch and worktree are retained for reference.

Draft 2/n of the Flash-Next implementation.

- [1/n Add Flash-Next model, FSDP and checkpoint reference coverage](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5782)
- [2/n Add tensor and expert parallelism with batched QSA teachers](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5783)
- [3/n Honor deterministic GDN normalization](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5784)
- [4/n Add pipeline stages, remat and numerical integration coverage](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5785)

Depends on [1/n](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5782).
Its review base is `users/shuhuayu/qwen3-8-fn-02-model`. After the parent lands,
rebase as needed and retarget this PR to `main` before merging.

@@ -73,6 +73,15 @@ def test_unsupported_attention_configs_are_explicit(config):
         build_model_config(
             "debugmodel", parallelism=ParallelismConfig(context_parallel_degree=2)
         )
+    for flavor in ("debugmodel", "debugmodel_mm", "125B-A6B"):
+        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="must divide QSA KV heads"):
+            build_model_config(
+                flavor,
+                seq_len=16,
+                parallelism=ParallelismConfig(
+                    tensor_parallel_degree=4, expert_parallel_degree=4
+                ),
+            )
     for indexer_ratio, attention_ratio in ((8, 4), (4, 8), (8, 8)):
         attention = copy.deepcopy(config.layers[3].attention)
         attention.indexer.compress_ratio = indexer_ratio
@@ -642,3 +651,126 @@ def test_optimizer_resets_auxiliary_losses_once_with_remat(config):
         AuxLoss._group_counts.update(saved_counts)
         AuxLoss.group_acc.clear()
         AuxLoss.group_acc.update(saved_acc)
+
+
+def test_qsa_teacher_packets_preserve_tail_and_tp_gradient_scaling():
+    from torch.nn.attention import sdpa_kernel, SDPBackend
+    from torchtitan.models.qwen3_8_flash_next import attention as qsa
+
+    torch.manual_seed(42)
+    T, R, B, H, K = 273, 4, 3, 2, 4
+    J = B * R + R - 1
+    indices = torch.full((T, J), -1, dtype=torch.long)
+    for i in range(T):
+        complete = min((i + 1) // R, B)
+        if complete:
+            indices[i, : complete * R] = torch.arange(complete * R)
+        tail = (i + 1) % R
+        if tail:
+            indices[i, B * R : B * R + tail] = torch.arange(i + 1 - tail, i + 1)
+    indices[::97] = -1
+    scores = torch.randn(T, B)
+    invalid_blocks = indices[:, : B * R].reshape(T, B, R)[:, :, 0] < 0
+    scores = scores.masked_fill(invalid_blocks, -torch.inf).requires_grad_()
+    oracle_scores = scores.detach().clone().requires_grad_()
+    query = torch.randn(T, H, K, requires_grad=True)
+    key = torch.randn(T, 1, K, requires_grad=True)
+    value = torch.randn(T, 1, K, requires_grad=True)
+    remote_query = torch.randn(T, H, K)
+    remote_key = torch.randn(T, 1, K)
+    scale = K**-0.5
+
+    def teacher_chunk(q, k, start, stop):
+        selected = indices[start:stop]
+        valid = selected >= 0
+        q_chunk = q[start:stop].unsqueeze(2)
+        keys = k[selected.clamp_min(0)].transpose(1, 2).repeat_interleave(H, 1)
+        logits = (q_chunk.float() * keys.float()).sum(-1) * scale
+        logits = logits.masked_fill(~valid[:, None], torch.finfo(torch.float32).min)
+        return logits.softmax(-1).sum(1) / (2 * H) * valid
+
+    remote_chunks, expected_outputs = [], []
+    expected_raw_sum = oracle_scores.new_zeros(())
+    with torch.no_grad():
+        local_teachers = [
+            teacher_chunk(query, key, start, start + 16) for start in range(0, T, 16)
+        ]
+        remote_teachers = [
+            teacher_chunk(remote_query, remote_key, start, start + 16)
+            for start in range(0, T, 16)
+        ]
+        for start in range(0, T, 16):
+            selected = indices[start : start + 16]
+            with sdpa_kernel(SDPBackend.MATH):
+                expected_outputs.append(
+                    F.scaled_dot_product_attention(
+                        query[start : start + 16].unsqueeze(2),
+                        key[selected.clamp_min(0)].transpose(1, 2),
+                        value[selected.clamp_min(0)].transpose(1, 2),
+                        attn_mask=(selected >= 0)[:, None, None],
+                        scale=scale,
+                        enable_gqa=True,
+                    ).squeeze(2)
+                )
+        for start in range(0, len(remote_teachers), 16):
+            remote_chunks.append(
+                torch.cat(
+                    [chunk[:, : B * R] for chunk in remote_teachers[start : start + 16]]
+                )
+            )
+    for chunk_index, start in enumerate(range(0, T, 16)):
+        teacher = local_teachers[chunk_index] + remote_teachers[chunk_index]
+        blocks = teacher[:, : B * R].unflatten(-1, (B, R)).amax(-1)
+        expected_raw_sum = expected_raw_sum + qsa.QSAIndexerLoss.block_kl(
+            oracle_scores[start : start + 16], blocks
+        )
+
+    inner = (
+        qsa.QSAInnerAttention.Config(
+            compress_ratio=R,
+            num_heads=2 * H,
+            indexer_loss=qsa.QSAIndexerLoss.Config(coeff=1.0, reduce_mesh="loss"),
+        )
+        .build()
+        .train()
+    )
+    communication_shapes, captured = [], []
+    original_inject = inner.indexer_loss.inject
+
+    def collective(local, operation, group):
+        assert operation == "sum"
+        remote = remote_chunks[len(communication_shapes)]
+        assert local.shape == remote.shape
+        communication_shapes.append(list(local.shape))
+        return local + remote
+
+    def inject(raw_sum, **kwargs):
+        captured.append(raw_sum)
+        return original_inject(raw_sum, **kwargs)
+
+    with patch.object(qsa, "spmd_mesh_group", return_value=object()), patch.object(
+        qsa, "spmd_mesh_size", return_value=2
+    ), patch.object(qsa, "all_reduce", side_effect=collective), patch.object(
+        qsa, "wait_tensor", side_effect=lambda x: x
+    ), patch.object(
+        inner.indexer_loss, "inject", side_effect=inject
+    ):
+        output = inner(
+            query,
+            key,
+            value,
+            selected_indices_TJ=indices,
+            scores_TB=scores,
+            scale=scale,
+            enable_gqa=True,
+            aux_loss_denominator=torch.tensor(float(T)),
+        )
+
+    assert communication_shapes == [[256, 12], [17, 12]]
+    torch.testing.assert_close(output, torch.cat(expected_outputs), atol=0, rtol=0)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(captured[0], expected_raw_sum, atol=0, rtol=0)
+    actual_grad = torch.autograd.grad(output.sum() * 0, scores)[0]
+    expected_grad = torch.autograd.grad(
+        expected_raw_sum * ((1.0 / T) / 2), oracle_scores
+    )[0]
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual_grad, expected_grad, atol=0, rtol=0)

+from torch.distributed._functional_collectives import all_reduce, wait_tensor
